data.gender_notes: Yevania is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Greek, Yevania is derived from the Greek word 'Yevos' which means 'Jehovah' and 'ania' meaning 'grace'. In the Bible, this name is associated with the wife of King David, who was a woman of great beauty and grace. She was also known for her loyalty and faithfulness to her husband and to God. The name Yevania carries the meaning “Jehovah's Grace” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Yevania usually hope their child will grow to embody jehovah's grace and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: The name Yevania is believed to have originated from the Byzantine Empire, specifically the region of Georgia. It is suggested that the name may have been derived from the Georgian word 'evandar', meaning 'bringer of good news'. This theory is supported by the fact that the region was a significant producer of wine, and the name may have been associated with the Christian concept of 'good news' or 'gospel' brought by the wine.

Later, during the Crusades, the name Yevania was used to refer to the principality of Galilee. This usage is attributed to the fact that the region was under the rule of a Greek nobleman named Evan, who held the title of 'Prince of Yevania'. The name may have also been influenced by the Greek word 'evanghelia', meaning 'gospel'.
